detail.text: Only an effective result with explicit constants can narrow a statement whose remaining cases are concrete (n > 10^6, value > 10^60). Ineffective results cannot: a hole 'there is T such that collisions of value ≥ T have shape X' leaves a remainder that must hold for every T, which is the core again. That rules out Siegel/Beukers–Shorey–Tijdeman per-pair finiteness, Brindza's superelliptic finiteness and MRSTT 2022 Thm 1.3 ('t sufficiently large') as narrowings here. Effective inputs used on 202…

route.text: Narrow the core by effective results only: Yamada 2020 Thm 1.1 (PR #1172), then on its remainder an elementary prime-interval separation with the prime-gap theorems of Nagura 1952 and Schoenfeld 1976 as cited holes.

literature_proposed.summary: Open. The residue of de Weger's conjecture after everything proved: no collision C(n,k) = C(m,l) (2 ≤ k ≤ n/2, 2 ≤ l ≤ m/2, k < l) with (k,l) outside the nine solved pairs, not of the shapes (n−1,k+1), (n−1,k+2), (n−2,k+1), with n > 10^6 and C(n,k) > 10^60. Nothing published is left to peel; what is missing is a bound uniform in (k,l). A proof closes the whole --h2 branch and, with MRSTT Theorem 1.3, Singmaster's conjecture.
